source.title: A Revision of Neural Tangent Kernel-based Approaches for Neural Networks
source.authors: Kyungsu Kim; A. Lozano; Eunho Yang

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper’s own theoretical results argue that cited NTK training-error guarantees fail when the network scaling factor decreases with sample size; it then revises the bounds for constant scaling. It does not run random-label experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper gives theoretical results about training-error guarantees for general labels, not experiments applying random labels. It cites prior work on random-label learning and slower training, but those cited results are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The paper revises NTK guarantees for generic-label regression under particular width and scaling assumptions. Its counterexample concerns a contraction bound, not failure to fit completely random labels. Its revised bound does not establish V1's random-label behavior under unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters. Statements about slower random-label learning are attributed to prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors argue that decreasing initialization or output scaling invalidates several existing NTK guarantees, attribute this to shrinking trained outputs, and propose revised bounds using constant scaling. These are their theoretical conclusions, not observed failures of random-label fitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and revises theoretical NTK bounds for gradient-descent training and generalization; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments or use their empirical procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical conclusions depend on the network scaling factor κ: the paper reports counterexamples when κ decreases with n and revised guarantees for κ = Θ(1).

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2.2 states that a cited geometric residual-contraction guarantee fails at some finite iteration when initialization scale decreases with sample size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Certain NTK convergence-rate guarantees require qualification concerning initialization scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2.3 and Proposition 2 give a revised generic-label training-residual bound that approaches zero as iterations and sample size increase, with constant initialization scale and sufficiently growing width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under specified overparameterization assumptions, constant initialization scaling permits a vanishing NTK training-residual bound.

record.problems: The evidence on the claim is theoretical rather than empirical and uses generic labels, not random labels. It does not measure test error, chance performance, shuffled or noise inputs, optimizer-time comparisons, regularization, or learning order.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling fitted by standard stochastic-gradient training with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, together with chance-level test performance.
Training-time ratio for random versus true labels and slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V1 verdicts. Failure of a convergence-rate guarantee does not establish failure of eventual fitting, and untested claim components do not justify limits_scope.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test completely random labels, chance-level test error, or empirical fitting by standard stochastic-gradient training. Its theoretical counterexample concerns a decreasing output or initialization scale and generic labels.
The paper does not compare training time for true and random labels or measure convergence slowdown as label corruption increases.
The paper does not train on shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper does not sweep the fraction of corrupted labels or report training and test error across corruption levels.
The paper does not test weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their effects on generalization.
The paper does not measure learning order or compare learning real and random labels over training.

rows.subject: two-layer, ReLU-activated, and scalar output neural network fW,a
rows.size_stated: m hidden neurons; m = Ω(n^(3−2γ)) in Theorem 2.2
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of discrete-time gradient descent training; Theorem 2.2 gives a counterexample to the cited training-error contraction guarantee when κ decreases with n.

conditions.value: generic y; theorem assumes ||y|| = O(√n), not random labels

rows.measure: Training residual contraction relative to the claimed gradient-descent bound
rows.baseline: Theorem 2.1 claims ||y − u(k+1)||² ≤ (1 − ηλ0/2)||y − u(k)||² for all k ≥ 0.
rows.value: Theorem 2.2 states there exists a finite k for which ||y − u(k+1)||² > (1 − ηλ0/2)||y − u(k)||², with probability at least 1 − δ.
rows.uncertainty: Probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization; δ ∈ (0,1).
rows.note: This theoretical counterexample challenges the guarantee under decreasing κ; it does not establish that a network empirically fails to fit random labels.
rows.check: Violating the stated residual contraction rate does not establish nonzero final training error or failure to fit random labels. Labels are generic and initialization scaling decreases with sample size. Replace the V1 link and partial state; retain only as a related theoretical result.

rows.subject: two-layer, ReLU-activated, and scalar output neural network fW,a
rows.operation_detail: Revised theoretical training-error bound for gradient descent under constant κ.
rows.measure: Whether the right-hand side of the revised training-error bound converges to zero as iteration number and sample size increase
rows.baseline: The original Corollary 2.1 bound includes a κ/δ term; the paper says that bound can fail to guarantee zero training loss under decreasing κ.
rows.value: The paper states the revised bound’s right-hand side converges to zero as k and n increase under the stated conditions.
rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization; δ ∈ (0,1).
rows.note: A theoretical result for constant scaling and generic labels; it does not test random-label fitting or empirical training.
rows.check: The revised generic-label regression bound approaches zero jointly with iterations and sample size under a prescribed growing-width condition and constant initialization scale. This is not a result on the full V1 behavior with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters; partial incorrectly treats untested components as an incomplete effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Decreasing κ with n in the theoretical setting of Theorem 2.2
reader_labels.reason: Theorem 2.2 gives a finite step violating the claimed contraction guarantee; this challenges the zero-training-error guarantee in this setting (R1).
